subject: Potential user-data exposure — timeline & evidence request
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@findata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Potential user-data exposure — timeline & evidence request

Hannah / Neha,

Sorry to drop this first thing — our security team flagged anomalous outbound transfers from a Redshift schema that contains a subset of user profiles used in our personalization product. We don’t have a full root cause yet, but we need to start the notification process.

Can you please confirm the following as soon as possible:
- What your incident-notification timeline is once Redwood confirms a constituent data exposure (we need contractual commitment and actual operational timeframe).
- What scope you will provide (log exports, sample records, file digests, hashes, indicators of compromise).
- Which subprocessors touched the affected dataset within the last 30 days and whether transfers involved any third-party analytics or caching providers (name + region + purpose).

We’ve attached a short summary from our detection team. We’ll stand up a bridge if helpful.

Attachment: prelim_incident_summary.pdf (1 page)

Thanks,

Alice Nguyen
Senior Security Program Manager
FinData Analytics
alice@findata.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0184
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@findata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential user-data exposure — timeline & evidence request

Alice — thanks for the heads-up and for the summary. We’ll prioritize this. High-level answers below; I’ll loop Neha (privacy & legal) for the contractual specifics and Marissa on ops.

1) Notification timeline: Redwood’s internal playbook is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects customer data. In practice, we aim to provide an initial factual notification within 24 hours of confirmation and an investigative update within 72 hours. We will not delay notification pending full root-cause.

2) Scope & evidence: We can provide:
   - Timestamped extracts of access logs relevant to the affected resources (S3/Redshift query logs)
   - Lists of object keys and associated digests (SHA256) for exported files
   - A summary of actions taken (revoked credentials, revoked keys, snapshot of ACL changes)
   - Redacted sample records where required for verification (we’ll coordinate the redaction approach)

3) Subprocessors & transfers: We will provide a list of subprocessors with the role and region. Preliminary note: our runtime caching partner (CloudEdge Inc.) may have processed derived request-level caches; we’ll confirm scope and retention window. For cross-border transfer legal basis: DPA references SCCs and documented transfer impact; Neha will confirm the applicable mechanism.

Next steps:
- Neha, can you prepare the exact contractual references (DPA section numbers) and confirm whether we can deliver the raw log extracts to FinData under the current DPA?
- Ops (Marissa), please gather a 30-day access log excerpt and one sample Redshift query result set for correlation.

I’ll schedule a 30-minute bridge for 11:30 PT if that works for everyone.

Attachment: redwood_incident_response_checklist.docx (internal checklist)

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@findata.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinData Security <security@findata.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential user-data exposure — timeline & evidence request

Hannah — that plan works. For clarity: FinData requires at minimum the following to support our regulator notice assessment:
- MD5/SHA hashes for any exported files so we can confirm matches to data we observed
- A sample of up to 10 records (PII redacted where possible) and a schema map so we can map columns to our internal identifiers
- Confirmation if any subprocessors exported the dataset outside the EEA (we’ll need country and provider)

We’re ready for the 11:30 PT bridge — I’ll send an invite to your calendar.

Thanks,
Alice
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@findata.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential user-data exposure — timeline & evidence request

Alice / Hannah / Marissa — following up with the legal/privacy specifics we discussed on the bridge. Per Redwood’s DPA (v3):

- Incident notification clause: Redwood will provide "prompt notice" to customers of any confirmed security incident affecting customer data and will include known facts, mitigation steps taken, and planned next actions. Our operational target is initial factual notice within 24 hours of confirmation and a substantive update within 72 hours; this is consistent with section 4.2 of the DPA.

- Data export & evidence: We can furnish time-bounded log extracts and file digests. We will not disclose raw PII beyond redacted samples unless required for legal/regulatory obligation; however, we can provide hashed identifiers and redacted record samples for matching.

- Subprocessors: Attached is an export of subprocessors that interacted with customer datasets in the past 30 days. Note that some infrastructure subprocessors perform ephemeral caching or monitoring and do not persist customer records beyond 24 hours. We will explicitly label which processors performed exports or transfers.

- Transfers & legal basis: Redwood relies on SCCs for EEA→US transfers for platform telemetry and has documented transfer impact assessments. If FinData needs executed SCCs between specific subprocessors, we will coordinate through our contracts team and provide those artifacts where permitted.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa (Ops): provide S3/Redshift access log export + list of object keys (owner: Marissa) — ETA 3 hours.
- Hannah: confirm bridge minutes and initial notice text (owner: Hannah) — ETA 1 hour.
- Neha (Privacy): deliver DPA section references, subprocessor list with roles & regions, and a redaction plan for sample records (owner: Neha) — ETA 6 hours.

Attachment: s3_access_logs_excerpt.csv (log excerpt)
Shared drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/incident-findata-2026

If anyone needs narrower permissions for the drive, let me know and I’ll open a time-limited share.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
